extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and practitioners who represent parties before the USPTO (particularly trademark practitioners), OED staff, and counsel handling USPTO disciplinary matters
extracted.subtask_description: A final disciplinary order approving an affidavit of resignation and excluding a practitioner on consent under 37 CFR § 11.27, describing the factual acknowledgements required in the affidavit, the alleged rule violations, the Director's authority, publication requirements, and the prohibitions and conditions that accompany exclusion and potential reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to approve affidavit of resignation and exclude practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 CFR § 11.27, the USPTO Director has authority to approve an Affidavit of Resignation and to exclude a practitioner on consent from practice before the Office in all matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides the statutory and regulatory basis for approving resignations and issuing exclusions on consent; orders cite these provisions when accepting an affidavit of resignation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation requirements (37 CFR § 11.27(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit of resignation submitted for exclusion on consent must comply with 37 CFR § 11.27(a), including that the practitioner’s consent to exclusion be freely and voluntarily rendered, that the practitioner be represented by counsel, and that the practitioner be aware of the pending investigation and the legal/factual consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order reproduces the respondent's acknowledgements: (1) consent was voluntary and not coerced; (2) respondent was represented by counsel when making the affidavit; (3) respondent was aware an investigation under 37 CFR § 11.22 was pending and of the alleged misconduct; (4) respondent understands 37 CFR §§ 11.5(b), 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60; and (5) respondent consents to being excluded from practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner subject to USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 CFR § 11.1 and § 11.19(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'practitioner' practicing before the Office is subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct set forth at 37 CFR § 11.101 et seq., and practitioners are governed by the rules in 37 CFR § 11.19(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order identifies the respondent as a 'practitioner' pursuant to 37 CFR § 11.1 and cites § 11.19(a) as the source making the respondent subject to the rules; practitioners are expected to know and follow these rules when representing applicants or registrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to disclose all material facts in ex parte proceedings (37 CFR § 11.303(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: In an ex parte proceeding, a practitioner shall inform the tribunal of all material facts known to the practitioner that will enable the tribunal to make an informed decision, whether or not the facts are adverse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order alleges violation by not informing the Office that another person impersonated the practitioner, that that person was representing applicants without authority, and that the person forged the practitioner's signature on filings—facts material to trademark filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on assisting unauthorized practice of law (37 CFR § 11.505)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is professional misconduct for a practitioner to assist another in practicing law in a jurisdiction in violation of the regulation of the legal profession in that jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged misconduct includes allowing a non-U.S. attorney (CRTP) to impersonate the practitioner, access TEAS, represent trademark applicants under false pretenses, and forge the practitioner's signature—conduct the rule forbids assisting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation (37 CFR § 11.804(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: It is professional misconduct for a practitioner to engage in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order alleges that permitting impersonation and forged signatures for TEAS filings constitutes dishonesty/fraud/deceit or misrepresentation in violation of § 11.804(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice (37 CFR § 11.804(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: It is professional misconduct for a practitioner to engage in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order alleges that allowing impersonation and forged filings harmed the integrity of the federal trademark registration process and thus was prejudicial to the administration of justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on other conduct reflecting adversely on fitness to practice (37 CFR § 11.804(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: It is professional misconduct for a practitioner to engage in other conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged acts of permitting impersonation and forgery are cited as conduct reflecting adversely on fitness to practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervision and reasonable inquiry obligations (37 CFR § 11.18 and related expectations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must supervise non-attorney assistants and conduct an inquiry reasonable under the circumstances to support factual assertions presented to the USPTO; failure to supervise or to conduct a reasonable inquiry can lead to discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order references a line of disciplinary cases where practitioners were disciplined for not complying with USPTO rules, not adequately supervising non-attorney assistants, and failing to satisfy § 11.18 obligations; practitioners representing foreign-domiciled applicants are 'reasonably expected to know' these duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptions and consequences on reinstatement (37 CFR § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: By consenting to exclusion, the practitioner acknowledges that if and when he applies for reinstatement under 37 CFR § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume for the purpose of determining reinstatement that the facts and allegations in the investigation are true and that the practitioner could not have successfully defended against them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent acknowledged this presumption in the affidavit; the Final Order requires compliance with 37 CFR § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement and explains that reinstatement does not automatically restore prior account privileges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 CFR § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 CFR § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly orders compliance with § 11.58 (which governs resignation with pending disciplinary matters and related obligations) as a condition of the agreement and exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibitions and account restrictions following exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon exclusion, the practitioner shall be prohibited from applying for, obtaining, activating, verifying, sponsoring, or using any USPTO.gov or other USPTO filing system accounts for preparing or filing documents with the USPTO until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order authorizes disabling/suspending any USPTO.gov accounts associated with the respondent, prohibits assisting others in using USPTO systems, and lists specific prohibited acts (opening/activating accounts; applying for accounts; verifying others' credentials; sponsoring accounts) until reinstatement under § 11.60 is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: No automatic re-enabling of suspended/disabled accounts upon reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if reinstatement is granted, the USPTO is not obligated to re-enable or unsuspend any USPTO.gov accounts disabled or suspended pursuant to the Final Order; the practitioner must work with USPTO business units or acquire/create a new account in accordance with policies at that time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order clarifies that reinstatement does not automatically restore technical account access; responsibility for re-enabling or establishing accounts rests with the practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice requirements for disciplinary actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order in the OED FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice materially consistent with the order in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order prescribes public notice content summarizing the facts, alleged violations (citing specific CFR sections), and the nature of the exclusion; disciplinary decisions are posted at the OED Reading Room and in the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation that trademark practitioners (including those representing foreign-domiciled applicants) know implicated rules and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Attorneys who represent applicants, registrants, or others before the USPTO in trademark matters—including those representing foreign-domiciled applicants—are reasonably expected to know the provisions of the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct implicated by such representation and the potential disciplinary consequences when those provisions are violated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order explicitly states this expectation and lists illustrative prior disciplinary decisions to signal common bases for discipline (noncompliance with USPTO rules, inadequate supervision, failure to conduct reasonable inquiry).
